messages:
Alex M: Quick heads up — saw a regression on Qwen-34B (hosted) after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak. p95 generation latency +18%, throughput -22%. Root looks like paged KV fragmentation + wrong stride for MQA vs GQA.

Priya S: ugh. do we have a profiler trace? is it kernel-selection or batching heuristics?

Sam G: I grabbed a flamegraph from a repro run. short version: a lot more memcpy and page boundary stalls in the KV path, and kernels that should be using 'mqa_stride' got a gqa fallback path.

Sam G: profiler excerpt:```
Model: qwen-34b
Config: MQA, num_kv_heads=16, kv_dim=64
Throughput: 78 tok/s (baseline 100 tok/s)
Hot path: kv_read+kv_repack -> memcpy (42%), kernel_dispatch (30%)
Kernel chosen: gqa_generic_kernel (should be mqa_packed_kernel)
```

Jordan L: that points at the kernel selector mis-detecting head layout. recent change in selector uses heuristics on head_dim%64 and model tags. for mixtral/mistral variants rope scaling also changes base dims so heuristics might be brittle.

Priya S: can we force the kernel to mqa_packed and see if throughput returns? do an A/B with batch sizes too.

Sam G: did that locally: forcing mqa_packed brings perf back to ~98 tok/s. script I ran:```bash
export KERNEL_OVERRIDE=mqa_packed
python bench.py --model qwen-34b --batch 8 --seq 512 --kv-layout paged
```

Alex M: good sanity check. indicates selector bug. also saw higher fragmentation when num_key_value_heads != attention_heads/heads_per_kv (some models use interleaved mapping). paged layout exacerbates it.

Jordan L: reminder: RoPE scaling changes how positional dims map to KV layout for Mixtral and Mistral. if stride calc uses pure head_dim without scaling offset, we can end up with off-by-x that fragments pages.

perf-bot: CI run 2025-12-02T09:12:23Z — perf/regression — https://ci.redwood.internal/runs/5501 — p95 +17% matched locally :rotating_light:

Priya S: ok action plan: (1) add explicit model->layout mapping for known MQA/GQA variants (qwen/mixtral/mistral/llama family), (2) change selector to prefer packed MQA kernel when num_key_value_heads < attention_heads and kv_dim % 64 == 0, (3) add unit test for paged KV fragmentation case.

Sam G: I'll own (2) and the quick patch. Jordan can you enumerate models to hard-map? I can write tests and bench.

Jordan L: will dump model registry by EOD. early list: qwen-34b(mqa), qwen-7b(mqa fallback), mixtral-8x7b(gqa), mistral-7b(gqa-ish), llama-2-70b(gqa). also note some private fine-tuned variants with head dim tweaks.

Alex M: also check batching heuristics: observed that small batches (1-2) hit latency SLO but big batches (>=16) amplify fragmentation because batched KV writes cause more page splits. we should add an allocator hint to coalesce paged writes when batch_count > threshold.

Sam G: good call. I'll add a batching flag: KV_BATCH_COALESCE=true that groups KV updates per sharded page. microbench shows it reduces memcpy counts by ~30%.

Priya S: when you push patch, add a perf-run step in the PR that compares baseline vs patched with 3 configs: (A) qwen-34b mqa paged batch=8, (B) mixtral-8x7b gqa paged batch=8, (C) qwen-34b mqa paged batch=1. we need to prove no regressions for GQA path.

Sam G: noted. also found a subtle bug: kernel selector used integer division for head stride calc:``head_stride = head_dim / kv_head_factor`` which rounds down and can produce head_stride that doesn't align to 64. switching to ceil division fixes alignment decisions.

Jordan L: that explains off-by issues. once ceil is in, page fragmentation reduces. but still want explicit mappings for edge cases.

perf-bot: nightly-bench results queued: https://bench.redwood/internal/2025/12/02/patch-5501 — baseline vs patch (queued)

Alex M: quick FYI — RoPE scaling note: for models where RoPE scaling multiplies positional dims after kv packing, we must compute effective_kv_dim = kv_dim * rope_scale_factor before alignment checks. add that to selector.

Sam G: will implement ceil div + effective_kv_dim + forced-mqa-preference heuristics. planning a small rollback-safe flag: KERNEL_SELECTOR_STRICT=true to gate behavior in prod for 24h.

Priya S: please include changelog entry and add a perf-alert threshold for p95 > +10% on any model-route over 30m.

Jordan L: one more: for paged KV fragmentation we should instrument page occupancy and report percent_pages_with_cross_shard_writes in Runtime Console. helps SRE debug.

Alex M: agreed. add console metric and a short trace link in PR.

Sam G: patch out in an hour, will post PR link.

Priya S: thanks. if tests/bench pass, roll to canary with KERNEL_SELECTOR_STRICT=true then monitor. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: PR 5501 posted by Sam G — https://git.redwood/internal/pulls/5501 — auto-bench queued

Sam G: PR: https://git.redwood/internal/pulls/5501 — includes tests, ceil div fix, effective_kv_dim calc, KV_BATCH_COALESCE opt, and model-mapping for qwen/mixtral/mistral.

Alex M: will watch canary metrics. ping here if anything odd.

Jordan L: thanks everyone. follow-up meeting tomorrow 10am to review metric deltas.

Priya S: awesome work team.
